newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH SENDZIMIR STEEL MILL 1996 NET NOSEDIVES.
newsitem.headline: POLISH SENDZIMIR STEEL MILL 1996 NET NOSEDIVES.

text.p: Poland's largest steel mill Huta im. Sendzimira SA, preparing for privatisation, said its net profit plummeted to 14.3 million zlotys last year from 100 million in 1995, according to unaudited results.
The company said in a statement on Thursday that its 1996 gross profit was 17.6 million on sales of 2.9 billion zlotys. No comparative data was immediately available.
The firm, based near the southern city of Krakow and employing 17,500 workers, produced 2.5 million tonnes of steel last year.
The company's general manager Jerzy Knapik has earlier said that the lower profit resulted from harsh winter and a bad business climate in steel industry.
Under the company's privatisation plan, three daughter companies are to be carved out from Sendzimir and later privatised through sales of new shares to strategic investors.
Sendzimir needs about $200 million in investment to face foreign competition after Poland lifts barriers protecting its steel sector in the next several years.
